b_observe.label: lying
b_observe.source: coarse pass: one 640x480 frame every 10 s, YOLO11-small + ByteTrack, geometric label

c_question: This minute's confidence (0.395) is under the 0.45 trigger. Is 'lying' the right label for this minute, or was the box too weak to say?

d_verify.tool: higher-FPS re-examination window (3 fps, 4 s, tracker re-run on those frames)
d_verify.window_start: at 0 s, the start of the clip
d_verify.trigger: a box under 0.45 in the coarse pass
d_verify.tools_not_used: zoom/crop, cross-camera retrieval, a look-back or look-forward outside the 4 s window

f_learned: The label changed (lying to standing) and confidence rose to 0.828. The second read is better supported, but it is a new tracker pass matched by track number only, and at night the view is infrared with low contrast.
vlm: The VLM (Qwen2.5-VL-3B) was NOT invoked: its weights were not available on this machine. Verification used the tracker's box confidence plus the 3 fps temporal re-examination instead.
caveat: The tracker is reset before each pass (`track_frames` in src/detect.py), so the window's track numbers are issued again; the second read is matched to the first by track number and minute, not by a verified identity. Only the second-look row stays in activity.csv (the coarse row was dropped by dedup). Nothing here is a diagnosis.
